nodes.label: securityHeaders()
nodes.rationale: A helmet-style bundle - nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, COOP/CORP same-origin, and X-XSS-Protection: 0 because the legacy filter is buggy and off is safest. COEP, Permissions-Policy and HSTS are opt-in. It covers its whole subtree including rejections: an HttpError thrown by a layer below carries the headers out with it. CSP is deliberately excluded as too app-specific.

nodes.label: false omits a header, it does not remove one
nodes.rationale: The bundle only ever adds headers, and as a middleware it runs on top of what the backend already wrote - so contentTypeOptions: false leaves the backend's nosniff in place. Stopping it requires the server-wide withSecurityHeaders. There is no per-subtree opt-out deliberately: the backend's copy is the last word precisely so the responses no middleware sees are covered too - its own 404s, body-parse 413s, and the generic 500.

nodes.label: strictTransportSecurity
nodes.rationale: Emits HSTS on its own, default max-age 180 days plus includeSubDomains, set unconditionally because a browser ignores it over plain HTTP - so a dev server is a harmless no-op and framework servers usually sit behind a TLS-terminating proxy anyway. withPreload requires maxAge >= 1 year and includeSubDomains (the hstspreload.org rules, enforced at construction) because submitting to the preload list is hard to undo.
